name: Retail investors

subjectOf.text: Existing international proposals and guidelines on hedge fund valuation fail because they do not adequately distinguish between retail and qualified investors, and as of 2009 no legislature has issued an exhaustive set of rules addressing the factors that cause inaccurate valuation.
subjectOf.abstract: They also do not adequately distinguish between retail investors and qualified investors.11 So far, no legislature has issued an exhaustive set of rules to address the factors that lead to inaccurate valuation.
subjectOf.citation: Kaal, Hedge Fund Valuation Retailization, Regulation, and Investor Suitability (2009). SSRN: https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=1428387
scope_conditions: as of the time of writing, 2009

subjectOf.text: Although regulators and legislatures in many jurisdictions recognize that hedge fund issues affect retail investors, they have so far not addressed valuation and its interplay with retail investors.
subjectOf.abstract: So far, however, regulators and legislatures have not addressed the issue of valuation and its interplay with retail investors. The
subjectOf.citation: Kaal, Hedge Fund Valuation Retailization, Regulation, and Investor Suitability (2009). SSRN: https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=1428387
scope_conditions: as of 2009, across the surveyed jurisdictions

subjectOf.text: Retail investors are more likely to benefit from investor protection rules that optimize hedge fund valuation, because their minority position in the industry, the absence of informal rules, and management's lack of incentive to protect them leave them unprotected.
subjectOf.abstract: Given their minority position in the industry and the lack of informal rules and management's disincentives to protect their investments, retail investors are more likely to benefit from investor protection rules that optimize valuation of hedge funds.
subjectOf.citation: Kaal, Hedge Fund Valuation Retailization, Regulation, and Investor Suitability (2009). SSRN: https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=1428387
scope_conditions: retail investors in hedge funds and hedge fund like vehicles

subjectOf.text: Investor suitability standards are the author's preferred regulatory option because they would probably protect retail investors' interests without unduly burdening the hedge fund industry and other market participants.
subjectOf.abstract: Investor suitability standards seem the most preferable to this author because they would probably protect the interests of retail investors while at the same time not unduly burdening the hedge fund industry and other market participants.
subjectOf.citation: Kaal, Hedge Fund Valuation Retailization, Regulation, and Investor Suitability (2009). SSRN: https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=1428387
scope_conditions: compared against limiting complex products, raising qualification thresholds, mandating disclosure, and retail-level triggers

subjectOf.text: Limiting complex financial instruments in the portfolios of hedge funds open to retail investors, triggered once retail commitments exceed a set level of assets under management, would likely protect retail investors while limiting undue burdens on the industry.
subjectOf.abstract: limiting complex financial instruments in portfolios of hedge funds open to retail investors, if commitments from retail investors exceed some level of assets under management, would likely protect the interests of retail investors while at the same time limiting undue burdens for the industry.
subjectOf.citation: Kaal, Hedge Fund Valuation Retailization, Regulation, and Investor Suitability (2009). SSRN: https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=1428387
scope_conditions: where retail commitments exceed a threshold such as 20 percent of assets under management

subjectOf.text: A retail investor asset threshold would be gamed: managers would be incentivized to keep retail assets under the applicable threshold, thereby keeping the fund in the existing regulatory scheme without implementing additional retail investor protection.
subjectOf.abstract: Managers would be incentivized to keep the assets from retail investors under the applicable retail investor asset threshold. Therefore, they would keep the fund in the current regulatory scheme without implementing additional protection for retail investors. Arguably, this would at least make
subjectOf.citation: Kaal, Hedge Fund Valuation Retailization, Regulation, and Investor Suitability (2009). SSRN: https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=1428387
scope_conditions: where regulation is triggered by a retail asset threshold

subjectOf.text: The go anywhere features of unconstrained mutual funds impede a retail investor's ability to ascertain and understand what the fund is invested in and what risks those investments carry.
subjectOf.abstract: However, these "go anywhere" features may impede a retail investor's ability to ascertain and understand the UMF's investments, and the risks associated with those investments.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Unconstrained Mutual Funds and Retail Investor Protection (2016). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2811729
scope_conditions: retail investors relying on fund disclosures

subjectOf.text: Three features make it uniquely challenging for retail investors to evaluate the risks of unconstrained mutual funds: the lack of standard benchmarks, the recent emergence of the fund type, and the diversity and complexity of the strategies and risk exposures involved.
subjectOf.abstract: the lack of standard benchmarks for UMFs, the recent emergence of UMFs as an investment asset type, and the diversity among and complexity of UMFs' strategies and risk exposures make it uniquely challenging for retail investors to evaluate the risks of investing in UMF securities.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Unconstrained Mutual Funds and Retail Investor Protection (2016). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2811729
scope_conditions: retail investors evaluating unconstrained mutual fund securities

subjectOf.text: Because unconstrained mutual funds comply with the Company Act, they may be marketed and sold to all classes of retail investors, including those with limited or even no experience investing in securities.
subjectOf.abstract: Compliance with the Company Act means that UMFs may be marketed and sold to all classes of retail investors, including retail investors who have limited, or even no, experience investing in securities.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Unconstrained Mutual Funds and Retail Investor Protection (2016). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2811729
scope_conditions: funds registered and compliant under the Investment Company Act

subjectOf.text: It is questionable whether retail investors typically have the experience or training to fully appreciate the risks disclosed in unconstrained mutual fund prospectuses.
subjectOf.abstract: First, it is questionable whether retail investors typically have the experience or training to fully appreciate the risks disclosed in UMF prospectuses.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Unconstrained Mutual Funds and Retail Investor Protection (2016). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2811729
scope_conditions: average retail investors reading unconstrained fund prospectuses

subjectOf.text: Because an unconstrained mutual fund's performance is typically not assessed against any established benchmark, the retail investor must evaluate the fund without the contextual information routinely available for mutual funds pursuing more traditional credit strategies.
subjectOf.abstract: Therefore, it is left to the retail UMF investor to assess the fund's performance without the type of contextual information routinely available in relation to other mutual funds pursuing more "traditional" credit strategies.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Unconstrained Mutual Funds and Retail Investor Protection (2016). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2811729
scope_conditions: unconstrained funds that decline to adopt a benchmark

subjectOf.text: Retail investors may be led to believe that unconstrained mutual funds are safe relative to other fixed income mutual funds precisely because they are marketed, offered, and regulated as mutual funds, a risk that is unique to retail investors in these funds.
subjectOf.abstract: Retail investors may also be led to believe that UMFs are "safe" products relative to other fixed income mutual funds, because they are marketed, offered, and regulated as mutual funds. This is a risk that is unique to retail investors in UMFs.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Unconstrained Mutual Funds and Retail Investor Protection (2016). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2811729
scope_conditions: retail investors purchasing unconstrained funds through mutual fund channels

subjectOf.text: A retail investor's experience investing in traditional mutual funds is likely to be a poor indicator of whether that investor will understand the risks of investing in an unconstrained mutual fund.
subjectOf.abstract: Accordingly, retail investors' experience investing in "traditional" mutual funds is likely to be a poor indicator of whether a retail investor will understand the risks associated with investing in a UMF.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Unconstrained Mutual Funds and Retail Investor Protection (2016). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2811729
scope_conditions: retail investors extrapolating from prior traditional mutual fund experience

subjectOf.text: Capped ICO raises, adopted to address investor uncertainty about platform valuation in uncapped raises, backfire by creating strong incentives for investors to get in first and thereby raising the likelihood of retail investor frenzy.
subjectOf.abstract: However, capped ICO raises crate significant incentive for investors to attempt to get in first, raising the likelihood of retail investor frenzy.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Initial Coin Offerings The Top 25 Jurisdictions and Their Comparative Regulatory Responses (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3117224

subjectOf.text: Widespread retail investor trading of digital securities, including the ability to margin them, is the linchpin of survivability for blockchain based securities offerings; without retail access the technology may remain marginalized in the offering process.
subjectOf.abstract: will be the linchpin of survivability and evolution of blockchain-based securities offerings. Without retail investor access, the technology may remain marginalized in the offering process.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Samuel Evans, Blockchain-Based Securities Offerings (2019). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3411110
scope_conditions: retail investor access on a widespread basis

subjectOf.text: Capped ICO raises, adopted by the crypto community to reduce investor uncertainty about platform valuation in uncapped raises, backfire because the cap creates strong incentives for investors to get in first, raising the likelihood of retail investor frenzy.
subjectOf.abstract: However, capped ICO raises create significant incentives for investors to attempt to get in first, raising the likelihood of retail investor frenzy.
subjectOf.citation: Kaal, Digital Asset Market Evolution (2020). SSRN: https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=3606663

subjectOf.text: Retail investors, who hold roughly forty percent of U.S. equities and form a decisive voting bloc, are the channel through which LER strengthens incumbent board support in contested proxy battles.
subjectOf.abstract: By appealing to retail investors, who control roughly 40% of U.S. equities and form a powerful voting bloc,78 LER strengthens support for incumbent boards in contested proxy battles.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Liquid Equity Rewards in Corporate America (2025). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5583610
scope_conditions: contested proxy battles at U.S. issuers
